summary: A project page on the Finaltype foundry site for Monoflow, a humanist coding monospace. It reads like an illustrated article: a looping 3D laptop video, title, intro and a free-regular CTA, then dark navy SVG figures (styles on a monospace grid, an animated 'contextual repositioning' diagram, italics, diacritics) between short prose sections, an editable mock code editor, a poster carousel, a Fontspring buy box, author bios and the site footer. Its distinctive idea is explaining how letters shift inside fixed-width cells to improve monospace spacing.

A full-width pale-yellow band with a rendered white laptop floating at an angle, its screen showing a dark code editor set in Monoflow ('# Monoflow // enjoy the difference', 'import finaltype.de'); below on warm beige the title 'Monoflow' (~125px), an italic byline, a four-line intro in Monoflow and a small black 'Get the regular weight for free via Fontspring →' button (title area never cut as a block, attached to 01)
instances.ux: The 3D laptop video plays once on load (the laptop flies in and opens; at the end it closes flat); the button links out to Fontspring for the free Regular
instances.learn: Put the coding font where it will live: a rendered laptop screen with real-looking code says 'for programmers' before any copy
